title: Is 9.70 ± 0.04 consistent with 9.81?
caption: The measured g is 2.75000000000003 standard uncertainties from 9.81 m s⁻²: z = (9.81 − 9.7)/0.04 = 2.75000000000003. If 9.81 were right, chance alone would put the result this far away (in either direction) only about 0.6% of the time (the shaded tails), so at the 5% level the result is inconsistent: look for a systematic error.
alt: Standard normal curve with both tails beyond 2.75 standard deviations shaded; together they hold about 0.6 percent of the area.
description: Horizontal axis: z, the distance from the expected value in units of the standard uncertainty; the curve is the standard normal distribution.
The two shaded tails, beyond z = ±2.75, together hold p ≈ 0.006 of the area (two-sided).
p is below 0.05, so the difference is statistically significant: the measurement and 9.81 are inconsistent.
